read modulo $L$. The boundary of $f_{i,j}$ consists of
$h_{i,j},v_{i+1,j},h_{i,j+1},v_{i,j}$. Equivalently, this is the quotient of
the unit square tiling of $\mathbb R^2$ by translations in $L\mathbb Z^2$.

The cellulation has $L^2$ vertices, $2L^2$ edges, and $L^2$ faces. The
condition $L\ge3$ ensures that the four edges in each star and face are
distinct, and that every edge has two distinct endpoints and two distinct
incident faces. The vertex-edge graph joins vertices joined by an edge. The
face-adjacency graph joins faces sharing an edge; both graphs are connected.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered list of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces with specified ordered orthonormal bases of
sizes $d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1}$, allowing $d_k=0$. The elementary tensors of the
factor bases, ordered lexicographically, form an orthonormal basis of the
tensor register, and

$$\dim(H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1})=\prod_{k<n}d_k.$$

For the empty list the product is $1$ and the tensor space is $\mathbb C$; if
any $d_k=0$, the tensor space is zero and the product basis is empty.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S$ be a stabilizer subgroup generated by an ordered independent
Hermitian list $g_1,\ldots,g_r$. For a phase-aware Pauli error $E$, its
**syndrome** is the bit string $s(E)\in\mathbb F_2^r$ defined by

$$E g_j=(-1)^{s_j(E)}g_jE,\qquad s_j(E):=\omega(\lambda(E),\lambda(g_j)).$$

Here $\lambda(P(k,x,z))=(x,z)$ is the binary Pauli label and
$\omega((x,z),(x',z'))=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'$. The scalar center of
$\mathcal P_n$ is $Z_n=\{i^kI:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$, and the
**normalizer** is $N(S)=\{P\in\mathcal P_n:Pg=gP\text{ for every }g\in S\}$.
The **logical Pauli classes** form the quotient group

$$N(S)/(Z_nS).$$

A normalizer element is logically nontrivial exactly when it lies in
$N(S)\setminus Z_nS$. Multiplication by a scalar phase does not change a
syndrome or logical class.

$E_{r+1}=P_rE_r$, where each $P_r$ is $X$, $Y$, or $Z$ on a single edge and
the identity on every other edge.

For any prefix Pauli $E$, define its energy excess
$\varepsilon(E):=\langle E\psi,H_LE\psi\rangle-E_{\rm code}$, where
$E_{\rm code}:=-L^2(J_e+J_m)$ is the energy of every code vector. The
**Pauli-path energy barrier** of $Q$ is

$$\mathcal B_L(Q):=\min_{(E_0,\ldots,E_T)}\max_{0\le r\le T}\varepsilon(E_r),$$

where the minimum ranges over elementary Pauli paths to $Q$. This is a
finite-code energy quantity; it is not a thermal lifetime.

For the finite toric-code Hamiltonian
$H_L=-J_e\sum_q A_q-J_m\sum_f B_f$ with $J_e,J_m>0$, the ground space is
the four-dimensional toric code space and the ground energy is
$E_g=-L^2(J_e+J_m)$. The exact spectral gap above it is

a dual edge trail with no repeated edge and distinct endpoint faces

citations.quote:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$. Take the square grid with vertices $(i,j)$ for
$0\le i,j\le d$, unit horizontal and vertical edges, and $d^2$ square faces.
Let $R$ consist of the left and right vertical boundary edges together with
their vertices. The physical qubits are the edges not in $R$; there are
$2d^2$ such edges. Order vertices and faces lexicographically by their
coordinates, and order physical edges lexicographically by their lower
endpoint, with horizontal edges before vertical edges when endpoints tie.

Let $Q_0$ be the binary vector space on vertices outside $R$, $Q_1$ the
binary vector space on physical edges, and $Q_2$ the binary vector space on
faces. Define $\partial_1:Q_1\to Q_0$ by sending each physical edge to the
sum of its endpoints that are outside $R$. Define $\partial_2:Q_2\to Q_1$
by sending each face to its boundary with any edge in $R$ deleted.

The X-check matrix is $H_X=\partial_1$, with rows indexed by vertices
outside $R$ and columns by physical edges. The Z-check matrix is
$H_Z=\partial_2^{\mathsf T}$, with rows indexed by faces and columns by
physical edges. Thus X checks are the rows of $H_X$ and Z checks are the
rows of $H_Z$. The maps satisfy $\partial_1\partial_2=0$. The rough
boundaries are the left and right sides; the top and bottom are the
complementary dual boundaries.

For the relative $d\times d$ square patch of
[[def-qc-square-planar-surface-code]], the code encodes one logical qubit and
has stabilizer distance $d$. Every nontrivial Z logical class contains a
rough-to-rough path of length at least $d$, and a straight row attains $d$.
Every nontrivial X logical class contains a top-to-bottom dual path of length
at least $d+1$. For each $\ell\ge1$, the number of self-avoiding
rough-to-rough paths of length $\ell$ is at most $(d+1)3^\ell$.

For the periodic $L\times L$ toric stabilizer code with $L\ge3$, the
minimum weight of a normalizer Pauli outside the scalar-phase stabilizer is
$d(S)=L$.

For the periodic $L\times L$ toric checks with $L\ge3$, the common $+1$
eigenspace is a valid stabilizer code on $n=2L^2$ qubits. Its independent
check rank is $r=2L^2-2$, so its dimension is
$2^{n-r}=4=2^2$ and it encodes two logical qubits.

On the periodic torus, define four Pauli representatives

$$\bar Z_1=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z_L}Z_{h_{i,0}},\qquad \bar Z_2=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z_L}Z_{v_{0,j}},\qquad \bar X_1=\prod_{j\in\mathbb Z_L}X_{h_{0,j}},\qquad \bar X_2=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z_L}X_{v_{i,0}}.$$

The $\bar Z$ supports are the two fixed fundamental primal cycles. The
$\bar X$ supports are the dual cycles crossing them. These operators are
called the toric logical loops. As verified below, each is a nontrivial
logical Pauli class in the periodic toric code.

Thus both species have distance $3$; [F4] gives code dimension four. The distance profiles and code dimensions differ at the same linear size.

The reason is already present in the hypotheses: [F1] uses relative boundary maps and rough edges, while [F3] uses periodic incidence on a closed torus. Therefore planar boundary paths and their asymmetric distance theorem do not establish torus winding classes, check relations, or toric distance. The distinction is a finite combinatorial one and does not require a physical interpretation.
